content: Clarithromycin affects the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, leading to increased levels or effects of various drugs. Both clarithromycin and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or the use of alternative drugs. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate via CYP3A4 metabolism, with both drugs prolonging the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin and escitalopram each increase the toxicity of the other by prolonging the QTc interval. Escitalopram increases clarithromycin toxicity via QTc prolongation, and clarithromycin raises escitalopram levels or effects through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of estradiol, conjugated synthetic estrogens, estropipate, and etonogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of vonoprazan via CYP3A4 metabolism, while clarithromycin increases etravirine levels or effects through the same pathway. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of everolimus via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated. Fosphenytoin decreases vonoprazan levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases fedratinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. If the inhibitor is discontinued, increase the dose to 300 mg/day for two weeks, then to 400 mg/day as tolerated. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of felbamate and fentanyl (including intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal forms) via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. If coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses as needed. Clarithromycin increases fesoterodine levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin decreases fexinidazole levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Clarithromycin and fingolimod both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin and fluconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases fludrocortisone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin and fluphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases intranasal fluticasone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects. Monitor for signs of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-type symptoms. Clarithromycin increases fluvastatin toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which raises the risk of myopathy. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases fondaparinux effects by decreasing its metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin and formoterol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases fosamprenavir and fosaprepitant levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases futibatinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase futibatinib toxicities. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin and gadobenate both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. Clarithromycin and gemifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases gilteritinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating ECG monitoring if coadministered. Clarithromycin and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at initiation, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or changes from baseline by more than 60 ms. Clarithromycin increases glasdegib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation. Clarithromycin and granisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin increases haloperidol levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases heparin effects by decreasing its metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin increases hydrocortisone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases ibrutinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term, interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. Clarithromycin increases idelalisib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. If coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, monitor for idelalisib toxicity and adjust dosage as needed. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor and should not be coadministered with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Clarithromycin increases imipramine levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases indinavir levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin increases infigratinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin and inotuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor ECGs and electrolytes before and after initiation, and periodically during treatment. Clarithromycin increases irinotecan levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin and isoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin and isradipine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Itraconazole increases clarithromycin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin increases ivosidenib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. If coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. If the inhibitor is discontinued, increase the dose to 500 mg daily after at least five half-lives of the inhibitor. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or alternative therapies. Clarithromycin increases ixabepilone levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases ketamine levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Ketoconazole increases clarithromycin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases lapatinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin increases larotrectinib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin increases lefamulin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin increases lemborexant levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. Clarithromycin increases leniolisib levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Levoketoconazole increases clarithromycin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin and lithium both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin and lofepramine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin and lofexidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended. Clarithromycin and loperamide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is advised. Clarithromycin increases lopinavir levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir increases clarithromycin levels or effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoidance or alternative drug use is recommended.
